data.narrative:
Endurosat, a Series E space and aerospace company founded by Raycho Raychev, has raised $167M+ to date. The valuation landscape includes 5 public comparables (RKLB, PL, LUNR, ASTS, SATL) and 8 private peers spanning the sector, though narrow-stage peer multiples are insufficient for robust triangulation.

Stage-progression methodology, the only reliably applicable approach, anchors valuation to the company's $1.8B total-raised proxy and applies a 1.4x step-up multiplier typical of Series E advancement. This yields a median implied valuation of $2.5B. Peer-median analysis could not be applied: while 11 same-sector peers exist, none met the threshold of three or more datapoints within same-stage, adjacent-stage, or similar-valuation-tier filters. Public-comp anchoring via P/S multiples (6-ticker sector median of 23.9x) is inapplicable without disclosed revenue figures, standard for private companies.

The analysis supports a valuation range of $2.1B (low) to $2.9B (high), centered on $2.5B. This single-method result carries material uncertainty. Key unknowns include runway-to-profitability, customer concentration, and technology differentiation within the crowded smallsat payload and orbital servicing subsector. Validation through revenue-based metrics or expanded comparable transaction data would strengthen conviction.
